Nuclear NDT training in Charlotte: the short answer

Nuclear NDT training in Charlotte builds the method foundation that technicians need before a utility or outage contractor qualifies them for ASME Section XI in-service inspection at Carolinas nuclear stations. Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, live online or onsite at your facility, led by an ASNT Level III. It is a foundation, not CP-189 certification or EPRI PDI qualification.

We are blunt about that last point because nuclear is the sector where getting it wrong costs the most. Nuclear utilities typically require personnel certified under ANSI/ASNT CP-189 within a 10 CFR 50 Appendix B quality programme, and ultrasonic examiners on many Section XI scopes must pass a performance demonstration. No classroom course, ours included, replaces those steps. What good SNT-TC-1A training does is give technicians the physics, technique and documentation habits that make the nuclear steps achievable, and give employers a Level III-led foundation programme for their people.

Request a Charlotte nuclear NDT training quote, or read on.

Nuclear NDT work in Charlotte

Charlotte is the headquarters city of Duke Energy, which operates the largest regulated nuclear fleet in the United States. Two of its stations are close to the city: McGuire Nuclear Station on Lake Norman, north of Charlotte, and Catawba Nuclear Station on Lake Wylie in York County, South Carolina. Other Carolinas stations sit within a day's drive. We name these only as context for where nuclear NDT work happens; Atlantis has no relationship with Duke Energy and does not claim one.

Charlotte is also home to the EPRI laboratory campus on W.T. Harris Boulevard, including the EPRI NDE Center, which has worked on transferring inspection research into power-plant practice since the early 1980s. EPRI administers the industry's Performance Demonstration Initiative (PDI) for ultrasonic examination, which is why Charlotte appears so often in nuclear UT careers. Again, this is context: EPRI is not a training provider for this page's audience, and Atlantis is not affiliated with it.

The nuclear NDT work flowing through the metro falls into a few groups:

  • Refuelling outage inspection. Section XI in-service examinations of reactor coolant system welds, piping, nozzles and supports during scheduled refuelling outages, staffed largely by vendors and outage contractors.
  • Steam generator examination. Eddy current examination of steam generator tubing at pressurised-water reactors, with data acquisition and separately qualified data analysts.
  • Balance-of-plant and secondary-side work. Flow-accelerated corrosion programmes, heat-exchanger tubing, buried and above-ground piping, and structural examinations.
  • Nuclear-grade manufacturing and repair. Shops fabricating or repairing components to ASME Section III or under Appendix B quality programmes.

Fossil and gas plant work in the same region is covered on our power generation NDT training in Charlotte page.

For most people aiming at nuclear inspection, the UT Level II course is the single most important foundation, followed by the ET Level II course for steam generator work.

A method spotlight for Charlotte: UT on the road to performance demonstration

Ultrasonic examination dominates Section XI scope, and performance demonstration is what separates nuclear UT from general industry. Under ASME Section XI Appendix VIII, examiners and procedures must demonstrate they can detect and size real flaws in test specimens they have not seen before; the PDI programme administers that demonstration for US utilities. Candidates who pass tend to share a few habits: they understand beam physics well enough to explain why a signal looks the way it does, they can tell a geometric reflector from a flaw at a weld root or counterbore, they scan with disciplined coverage and index, and they size consistently. Those are exactly the things good SNT-TC-1A Level II training should build. We do not offer PDI preparation or claim PDI outcomes; we teach the foundation that makes later qualification realistic.

The SNT-TC-1A path, and where nuclear adds steps

  1. Employer written practice. SNT-TC-1A is employer-based. For nuclear vendors, the written practice often has to satisfy CP-189 and the utility's audit as well. See written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Method theory, equipment, technique and codes. Hours depend on method and level; see the training requirements matrix. CP-189 sets its own requirements.
  3. On-the-job experience. Logged under certified personnel; nuclear employers may require specific nuclear experience.
  4. General, specific and practical examinations. Administered by a Level III.
  5. Vision examination. Annually.
  6. Employer certification. Under SNT-TC-1A, or CP-189 for nuclear programmes.
  7. Nuclear overlays. Performance demonstration for applicable UT, site-specific training and plant access.

More on the employer side: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Plant access, radiation work and licensing

Working inside a nuclear plant's protected area requires unescorted access authorisation under NRC rules, which includes background checks, a fitness-for-duty programme with drug and alcohol testing, and plant-specific training, plus radiation worker training before entering radiologically controlled areas. These are arranged by the utility or the employing contractor, not by a training provider, and they take time; plan for them when hiring for an outage.

Industrial radiography is a separate matter. North Carolina is an NRC Agreement State, with radioactive materials licensed by the Radiation Protection Section of the state Department of Health and Human Services; South Carolina, where Catawba sits, runs its own state programme. Radiography inside a reactor facility can also involve NRC oversight. Check current requirements with the relevant agency before planning RT work. Atlantis teaches radiographic technique and interpretation; we do not issue radiation safety credentials.

How Atlantis delivers nuclear NDT foundation training to Charlotte

We have no training centre in Charlotte, and nothing on this page should be read as suggesting one. We deliver:

  • Onsite at your facility. Level III-led training at your Charlotte office, shop or training room, on your equipment and calibration standards, scheduled before outage mobilisation.
  • Live online. Real-time classroom sessions for individuals and dispersed crews. See online NDT training.
  • Blended. Online theory, then an onsite practical and examination block.

Refuelling outages run to tight schedules, and vendors staff up in the months before. We plan training backwards from your mobilisation dates. Ask about onsite training before your next outage; cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day. See also corporate NDT training.

What a foundation programme looks like for a Charlotte nuclear vendor

For a vendor hiring ahead of the outage season, a practical foundation programme usually has four parts. First, method classroom training in UT and ET for the people heading toward Section XI and steam generator scopes, with VT, MT and PT for the surface and visual crews. Second, practical sessions on the vendor's own calibration blocks and representative specimens, so technicians learn on the equipment they will carry into the plant. Third, Level III-administered examinations under the vendor's written practice, with records organised so the utility's auditors can trace every hour and every grade. Fourth, a clear hand-off to the steps we do not provide: CP-189 certification decisions by the employer, performance demonstration for Appendix VIII scopes, plant access and site-specific training. Done this way, new hires arrive at the utility's qualification steps with fewer gaps, and the vendor spends less of its outage budget on remedial training. We scope each programme around your written practice and your customers' requirements, and we say plainly where our part ends.

Level III services for Charlotte nuclear vendors and suppliers

Smaller vendors and suppliers in the nuclear supply chain often need outside Level III help: reviewing a written practice against CP-189 and a utility's audit checklist, preparing and administering examinations, reviewing procedures, and organising certification records so they survive an audit years later. Atlantis provides Level III services under SNT-TC-1A and can review documentation against CP-189 requirements, while your organisation retains responsibility for its Appendix B programme. For consulting, see nuclear NDT consulting in Charlotte, or book a Level III consultation.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments, useful for building scan discipline and indication recognition between sessions. It is practice only: it does not replace the practical exam on real specimens, and it is not a performance demonstration. Local users can start at Practical NDT for Charlotte.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, examinations and written-practice work.

Naval nuclear veterans in Charlotte

Former naval nuclear personnel often move into commercial nuclear work, and their experience with procedural compliance and radiological controls transfers well. NDT certification is still issued by the civilian employer, so the practical step is method training and documented experience. Our guide on moving from military inspection into ASNT certification covers this. GI Bill and WIOA funding generally goes only to approved schools; Atlantis does not claim that approval, so employer sponsorship is the usual route for our courses.

Frequently asked questions about nuclear NDT training in Charlotte

How do I get into nuclear NDT in Charlotte?

Most people certify in general industry first, usually in UT, then join a utility or Section XI vendor that certifies them under CP-189 and arranges performance demonstration and plant access.

Does Atlantis offer CP-189 or PDI training?

No. We train to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. CP-189 and PDI are explained here as context; your employer manages both.

Is SNT-TC-1A accepted at nuclear plants?

For safety-related Section XI work, utilities generally require CP-189. SNT-TC-1A is common for balance-of-plant, fabrication and non-safety-related work, and as a foundation.

What is PDI and do I need it?

PDI is the industry's Performance Demonstration Initiative, through which UT examiners and procedures demonstrate flaw detection and sizing under ASME Section XI Appendix VIII. You need it only for Appendix VIII-scoped UT, and your employer arranges it.

Which method should I learn for steam generator work?

Eddy current. ET Level II training is the foundation; steam generator data analysts then qualify separately under industry guidelines.

How long does UT Level II training take?

Under SNT-TC-1A it depends on the written practice: classroom hours plus on-the-job experience. See the training requirements matrix. CP-189 sets its own requirements.

Can I take nuclear NDT training online in North Carolina?

The classroom portion of SNT-TC-1A method training can be taken live online. Practical exams, performance demonstration and site training are always in person.

What does nuclear NDT training cost in Charlotte?

We quote on request. Cost depends on methods, levels, group size, delivery mode and whether exams and written-practice work are included. Onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Do I need security clearance to work at a nuclear plant?

You need unescorted access authorisation, which includes background checks and fitness-for-duty testing, arranged by the utility or your employer. It is separate from NDT certification.

Can you train our vendor crew before a refuelling outage?

Yes, for SNT-TC-1A foundation training, if we start early enough. Tell us your mobilisation dates.

What do nuclear NDT technicians earn?

We do not publish city salary figures. See our NDT salary guide for published ranges and sources.
